records.source: וַיְהִ֗י בְּאַחַ֤ת עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה בַּשְּׁלִישִׁ֖י בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָ֥ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And it was in [the] eleventh year, in the third [month], on [the] first of the month, came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: In the third month of the eleventh year, on its first day, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.1: And it came about in the eleventh year, in the third [month], on the first of the month, [that] the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

R.1: On the first day of the third month, in the eleventh year of our exile, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

decisions.choice: the eleventh year, the third month, the first day: June 587 BC
decisions.reason: Counted from Jehoiachin's exile, the date falls in June 587 BC (stated from general knowledge), about two months after 30:20, while Jerusalem was still under siege.

decisions.choice: the chapter: Pharaoh shown the fate of a great cedar
decisions.reason: Pharaoh is asked whom he is like (verse 2), and shown a great cedar, Assyria, which grew higher than every tree and was cut down (verses 3-14). Its fall shook the world and it went down to the world of the dead (15-17). The last verse names the lesson: "This is Pharaoh". Verses 2-9, the picture of the tree, are set in lines as poetry; the sentence on it (10-18) is prose.

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me, saying (L); came to me (B); The LORD gave me this message (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula. Readable puts the day first and says what the years are counted from, as in 20:1.

records.heading: A cedar in Lebanon

records.source: בֶּן־אָדָ֕ם אֱמֹ֛ר אֶל־פַּרְעֹ֥ה מֶֽלֶךְ־מִצְרַ֖יִם וְאֶל־הֲמוֹנ֑וֹ אֶל־מִ֖י דָּמִ֥יתָ בְגָדְלֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his multitude: Whom are you like in your greatness?
pieces: Son of man, say to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, and to his hordes: \q Who can be compared with you in your greatness?

L.2: Son of man, say to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, and to his multitude: \q Whom are you like in your greatness?

R.2: Son of man, say to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, and to all his people: \q Who is as great as you are?

decisions.choice: son of man: a mortal, as God addresses Ezekiel
decisions.reason: See the note at 2:1.

decisions.choice: his multitude: his crowds of people, his army and his pomp
decisions.reason: The word *hamon* (29:19) runs through the oracles on Egypt. Here it is the throng of people and soldiers who belong to Pharaoh.

decisions.choice: whom are you like?: a question answered at the end
decisions.reason: The question opens the oracle and returns in verse 18, where the answer is given.

decisions.choice: no quotation marks; lines from the question on
decisions.reason: What Ezekiel is told to say takes no quotation marks. The poem about the cedar begins with the question and follows the Hebrew accents for its lines.

records.source: הִנֵּ֨ה אַשּׁ֜וּר אֶ֣רֶז בַּלְּבָנ֗וֹן יְפֵ֥ה עָנָ֛ף וְחֹ֥רֶשׁ מֵצַ֖ל וּגְבַ֣הּ קוֹמָ֑ה וּבֵ֣ין עֲבֹתִ֔ים הָיְתָ֖ה צַמַּרְתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Look, Assyria [was] a cedar in Lebanon, beautiful of branches and a forest giving shade, and high of stature, and among [the] clouds was its top.
pieces: Consider Assyria, a cedar in Lebanon, with beautiful branches and shade like a forest, towering high, \q its top among the clouds.

L.3: Look, Assyria [was] a cedar in Lebanon, beautiful of branches, a shading forest, and high of stature, \q and among the clouds was its top.

R.3: Think of Assyria. It was like a cedar in Lebanon, with beautiful branches that gave shade like a forest. It was very tall, \q and its top reached the clouds.

decisions.choice: Assyria
alternatives: Look, a cypress, a cedar in Lebanon
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names Assyria, the empire that had ruled the world and fell when Nineveh was destroyed in 612 BC: Pharaoh is shown what happened to a power as great as his. With a small change the word becomes the name of a tree, the cypress or box tree (27:6), and the whole poem would describe Pharaoh himself as a tree. The Hebrew is kept.

decisions.choice: a cedar in Lebanon: the picture of a great king and empire
decisions.reason: The tallest trees picture kings and kingdoms (17:3, 22-23; Daniel 4:7-9).

decisions.choice: among the clouds
decisions.reason: The word may mean thick clouds or thick foliage; here it is the height the treetop reached (verses 10, 14).

decisions.choice: It was like a cedar
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture a comparison, as at 29:3.

records.source: מַ֣יִם גִּדְּל֔וּהוּ תְּה֖וֹם רֹֽמְמָ֑תְהוּ אֶת־נַהֲרֹתֶ֗יהָ הֹלֵךְ֙ סְבִיב֣וֹת מַטָּעָ֔הּ וְאֶת־תְּעָלֹתֶ֣יהָ שִׁלְחָ֔ה אֶ֖ל כָּל־עֲצֵ֥י הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃
records.gloss: Waters made it grow, [the] deep made it tall; its rivers were going around its planting place, and its channels it sent out to all [the] trees of the field.
pieces: The waters made it grow; the deep made it tall, \q sending its rivers all around the place where it was planted \q and its channels to all the trees of the field.

L.4: Waters made it grow; the deep made it tall; \q its rivers flowed all around its planting place, \q and its channels it sent out to all the trees of the field.

R.4: Plenty of water made it grow. Water from deep underground made it tall. \q Rivers flowed all around where it was planted, \q and streams went out to all the trees in the field.

decisions.choice: the deep: the great waters under the earth
decisions.reason: See 26:19. The tree drew on the waters of the deep, as Assyria drew its wealth from the great rivers of Mesopotamia.

records.source: עַל־כֵּן֙ גָּבְהָ֣א קֹמָת֔וֹ מִכֹּ֖ל עֲצֵ֣י הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וַתִּרְבֶּ֨ינָה סַֽרְעַפֹּתָ֜יו וַתֶּאֱרַ֧כְנָה פֹארֹתָ֛יו מִמַּ֥יִם רַבִּ֖ים בְּשַׁלְּחֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Therefore its height was high above all the trees of the field, and its boughs became many and its branches became long, from many waters when it sent [them] out.
pieces: So it grew taller \q than all the trees of the field. \q Its boughs grew many and its branches long because of the abundant water, as it spread its shoots.

L.5: Therefore its height towered \q above all the trees of the field, \q and its boughs multiplied and its branches grew long, because of many waters, as it sent [them] out.

R.5: So it grew taller \q than all the other trees. \q It had many large branches, and they grew long because it had so much water.

decisions.choice: as it sent them out: as the tree put out its shoots
decisions.reason: The words may mean the tree spreading its shoots, or the waters sending out their streams (verse 4).

records.source: בִּסְעַפֹּתָ֤יו קִֽנְנוּ֙ כָּל־ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְתַ֤חַת פֹּֽארֹתָיו֙ יָֽלְד֔וּ כֹּ֖ל חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וּבְצִלּוֹ֙ יֵֽשְׁב֔וּ כֹּ֖ל גּוֹיִ֥ם רַבִּֽים׃
records.gloss: In its boughs nested all [the] birds of the heavens, and under its branches gave birth all [the] beasts of the field, and in its shade dwelt all great nations.
pieces: All the birds of the sky nested in its boughs; \q under its branches all the wild animals gave birth to their young, \q and all the great nations lived in its shade.

L.6: In its boughs all the birds of the heavens made their nests, \q and under its branches all the beasts of the field gave birth, \q and in its shade dwelt all great nations.

R.6: All the birds nested in its branches. \q All the wild animals had their young under its branches. \q All the great nations lived in its shade.

decisions.choice: in its shade dwelt all great nations: the protection of an empire
decisions.reason: Shade is protection. The nations sheltered under Assyria's power, as birds and beasts under a tree (17:23; Daniel 4:9, 18). Jesus uses the picture of birds nesting in the branches in his parable of the mustard seed (Matthew 13:32).

records.source: וַיְּיִ֣ף בְּגָדְל֔וֹ בְּאֹ֖רֶךְ דָּֽלִיּוֹתָ֑יו כִּֽי־הָיָ֥ה שָׁרְשׁ֖וֹ אֶל־מַ֥יִם רַבִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And it was beautiful in its greatness, in [the] length of its branches, for its root was by many waters.
pieces: It was beautiful in its greatness, with its long branches, \q for its roots went down to abundant waters.

L.7: And it was fair in its greatness, in the length of its boughs, \q for its root was toward many waters.

R.7: It was a great and beautiful tree, with long branches, \q because its roots went down to plenty of water.

decisions.choice: its root by many waters: a well-watered tree
decisions.reason: The picture recalls the tree planted by streams of water in Psalm 1:3 and Jeremiah 17:8, but here the tree's strength leads to pride (verse 10).

records.source: אֲרָזִ֣ים לֹֽא־עֲמָמֻהוּ֮ בְּגַן־אֱלֹהִים֒ בְּרוֹשִׁ֗ים לֹ֤א דָמוּ֙ אֶל־סְעַפֹּתָ֔יו וְעַרְמֹנִ֥ים לֹֽא־הָי֖וּ כְּפֹֽארֹתָ֑יו כָּל־עֵץ֙ בְּגַן־אֱלֹהִ֔ים לֹא־דָמָ֥ה אֵלָ֖יו בְּיָפְיֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Cedars did not rival it in [the] garden of God; junipers were not like its boughs, and plane trees were not like its branches; every tree in [the] garden of God was not like it in its beauty.
pieces: The cedars in the garden of God could not match it, \q the junipers could not equal its boughs, \q and the plane trees were nothing like its branches; \q no tree in God's garden was its equal in beauty.

L.8: The cedars in the garden of God did not rival it; \q junipers were not like its boughs, \q and plane trees were not like its branches; \q no tree in the garden of God was like it in its beauty.

R.8: The cedars in God's garden were not as great. \q The junipers did not have boughs like it. \q The plane trees did not have branches like it. \q No tree in God's garden was as beautiful as it was.

decisions.choice: the garden of God: Eden
decisions.reason: See 28:13. The tree is greater than any tree in the garden God himself planted (Genesis 2:8-9).

decisions.choice: plane trees: tall spreading trees
decisions.reason: The tree named is probably the plane tree, which grows by water in the region (Genesis 30:37).

records.source: יָפֶ֣ה עֲשִׂיתִ֔יו בְּרֹ֖ב דָּֽלִיּוֹתָ֑יו וַיְקַנְאֻ֨הוּ֙ כָּל־עֲצֵי־עֵ֔דֶן אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּגַ֥ן הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃ס
records.gloss: Beautiful I made it in [the] abundance of its branches, and envied it all [the] trees of Eden that [were] in [the] garden of God.
pieces: I made it beautiful \q with its many branches, \q and all the trees of Eden, \q in the garden of God, envied it.

L.9: Beautiful I made it, \q with the abundance of its branches, \q and all the trees of Eden envied it, \q that [were] in the garden of God.

R.9: I made it beautiful, \q with so many branches. \q All the trees in Eden, \q the garden of God, were jealous of it.

decisions.choice: I made it beautiful: its greatness was the LORD's gift
decisions.reason: The LORD gave the tree its beauty. That makes its pride (verse 10) the more wrong.

records.source: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה יַ֕עַן אֲשֶׁ֥ר גָּבַ֖הְתָּ בְּקוֹמָ֑ה וַיִּתֵּ֤ן צַמַּרְתּוֹ֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ין עֲבוֹתִ֔ים וְרָ֥ם לְבָב֖וֹ בְּגָבְהֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Because you were high in height, and it set its top among [the] clouds, and its heart was lifted up in its height,
pieces: Therefore the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Because it grew so tall, setting its top among the clouds, and its heart grew proud of its height,

L.10: Therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Because you were lofty in height, and it set its top among the clouds, and its heart was lifted up in its height,

R.10: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: The tree grew very tall, and its top reached the clouds. It became proud because it was so tall.

decisions.choice: you were lofty ... it set its top: a change of person
decisions.reason: The Hebrew begins with "you", speaking to Pharaoh, then goes on with "it", the tree. The words for Assyria are also meant for Pharaoh. Some ancient translations read "it" throughout (stated from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: its heart was lifted up: pride before a fall
decisions.reason: The fall of the proud is a theme of the Tyre and Egypt oracles (28:2, 5, 17) and of Isaiah 2:12-13 and Daniel 4:27-34.

decisions.choice: it grew so tall (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep to the tree, which the rest of the sentence speaks of, so that the reader is not confused by the change of person (m1).

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula.

records.heading: The great tree cut down

records.source: וְאֶ֨תְּנֵ֔הוּ בְּיַ֖ד אֵ֣יל גּוֹיִ֑ם עָשׂ֤וֹ יַֽעֲשֶׂה֙ ל֔וֹ כְּרִשְׁע֖וֹ גֵּרַשְׁתִּֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And I gave it into [the] hand of [the] mighty one of [the] nations; he will surely deal with it; according to its wickedness I drove it out.
pieces: I handed it over to the mightiest of the nations, who dealt with it as its wickedness deserved. I drove it out.

L.11: so I gave it into the hand of the mighty one of the nations; he would surely deal with it; for its wickedness I drove it out.

R.11: So I handed it over to the strongest ruler of the nations. He punished it for its evil, as it deserved. I threw it out.

decisions.choice: the mighty one of the nations: the conqueror of Assyria
decisions.reason: The word means a ram, a leader, or a mighty one. Babylon, with the Medes, destroyed Nineveh in 612 BC and ended the Assyrian empire (stated from general knowledge). The same Babylon now threatens Egypt.

decisions.choice: mixed tenses: the fall told as done and as certain
decisions.reason: The Hebrew mixes past and future verbs. The fall of Assyria is past; the words also look ahead to Pharaoh's fall.

records.source: וַיִּכְרְתֻ֧הוּ זָרִ֛ים עָרִיצֵ֥י גוֹיִ֖ם וַֽיִּטְּשֻׁ֑הוּ אֶל־הֶ֠הָרִים וּבְכָל־גֵּ֨אָי֜וֹת נָפְל֣וּ דָלִיּוֹתָ֗יו וַתִּשָּׁבַ֤רְנָה פֹֽארֹתָיו֙ בְּכֹל֙ אֲפִיקֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ וַיֵּרְד֧וּ מִצִּלּ֛וֹ כָּל־עַמֵּ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ וַֽיִּטְּשֻֽׁהוּ׃
records.gloss: And strangers, [the] ruthless of [the] nations, cut it down and left it; on the mountains and in all [the] valleys its branches fell, and its boughs were broken in all [the] ravines of the land; and went down from its shade all [the] peoples of the earth and left it.
pieces: Foreigners from the most ruthless of nations cut it down and left it lying. Its branches fell on the mountains and in every valley, and its boughs lay broken in all the ravines of the land. All the peoples of the earth came out from its shade and left it.

L.12: And strangers, the ruthless of the nations, cut it down and abandoned it; on the mountains and in all the valleys its branches fell, and its boughs were broken in all the ravines of the land; and all the peoples of the earth went down from its shade and abandoned it.

R.12: Foreigners from the cruelest nation cut it down and left it there. Its branches fell on the mountains and in all the valleys. Its broken branches lay in all the ravines of the land. All the nations of the earth left its shade and went away.

decisions.choice: the ruthless of the nations: Babylon
the peoples went down from its shade: its allies abandoned it
decisions.reason: Those who had sheltered under the empire left it when it fell.

records.source: עַל־מַפַּלְתּ֥וֹ יִשְׁכְּנ֖וּ כָּל־ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְאֶל־פֹּארֹתָ֣יו הָי֔וּ כֹּ֖ל חַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃
records.gloss: On its fallen trunk dwell all [the] birds of the heavens, and on its branches are all [the] beasts of the field.
pieces: All the birds of the sky settle on its fallen trunk, and all the wild animals live among its branches.

L.13: On its fallen trunk all the birds of the heavens dwell, and among its branches are all the beasts of the field.

R.13: Birds sit on its fallen trunk, and wild animals live among its broken branches.

decisions.choice: the birds and beasts of verse 6, now on the fallen tree
decisions.reason: The creatures that sheltered in the living tree now perch on its fallen trunk, as scavengers on a corpse (32:4).

records.source: לְמַ֡עַן אֲשֶׁר֩ לֹא־יִגְבְּה֨וּ בְקוֹמָתָ֜ם כָּל־עֲצֵי־מַ֗יִם וְלֹֽא־יִתְּנ֤וּ אֶת־צַמַּרְתָּם֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ין עֲבֹתִ֔ים וְלֹֽא־יַעַמְד֧וּ אֵלֵיהֶ֛ם בְּגָבְהָ֖ם כָּל־שֹׁ֣תֵי מָ֑יִם כִּֽי־כֻלָּם֩ נִתְּנ֨וּ לַמָּ֜וֶת אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ תַּחְתִּ֗ית בְּת֛וֹךְ בְּנֵ֥י אָדָ֖ם אֶל־י֥וֹרְדֵי בֽוֹר׃ס
records.gloss: so that they will not be lifted up in their height, any trees of water, and not set their top among [the] clouds, and not stand up their mighty ones in their height, any drinkers of water; for all of them have been given to death, to [the] earth below, in [the] midst of [the] sons of humankind, with [those who] go down [to the] pit.
pieces: This happened so that no other trees by the waters would grow proud of their height or lift their tops among the clouds, and no well-watered tree would rise to such height. For all of them are destined for death, for the world below, among mortals, with those who go down to the pit.

L.14: [This was] so that none of the trees by the waters would be lofty in their height or set their top among the clouds, and that their mighty ones would not stand up in their height, all that drink water; for all of them are given over to death, to the earth below, in the midst of the {{gender:children|sons}} of humankind, with those who go down to the pit.

R.14: This happened so that no other tree growing by water would become proud of being tall or lift its top to the clouds. No tree with plenty of water should ever think it can grow that tall. All of them are going to die. They will go down to the world below, with all other human beings, with those who go down to the pit.

decisions.choice: a warning to every power
decisions.reason: The cedar's fall is a lesson for all the "trees", the kings and nations, so that none grows proud of its greatness.

decisions.choice: the earth below: the world of the dead
decisions.reason: See 26:20. The phrase returns in verses 16 and 18 and in 32:18 and 24.

decisions.choice: among mortals, with those who go down to the pit: the picture gives way to its meaning
decisions.reason: The trees are said to die among human beings, because they stand for kings and peoples. "The pit" is the grave (26:20).

decisions.choice: the children of humankind (L, gender default); mortals (B); human beings (R)
decisions.reason: *Bene 'adam*, humankind set against God, follows the settled wording, with the gender setting at Literal.

records.source: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה בְּי֨וֹם רִדְתּ֤וֹ שְׁא֨וֹלָה֙ הֶאֱבַ֜לְתִּי כִּסֵּ֤תִי עָלָיו֙ אֶת־תְּה֔וֹם וָֽאֶמְנַע֙ נַהֲרוֹתֶ֔יהָ וַיִּכָּלְא֖וּ מַ֣יִם רַבִּ֑ים וָאַקְדִּ֤ר עָלָיו֙ לְבָנ֔וֹן וְכָל־עֲצֵ֥י הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה עָלָ֥יו עֻלְפֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: On [the] day it went down to Sheol I caused mourning; I covered over it the deep, and I held back its rivers, and were restrained [the] many waters; and I made Lebanon mourn for it, and all [the] trees of the field for it fainted.
pieces: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: On the day it went down to Sheol, I made the deep mourn for it and covered it over. I held back its rivers, and its great waters were stopped. I dressed Lebanon in gloom for it, and all the trees of the field wilted because of it.

L.15: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: On the day it went down to Sheol I caused mourning; I covered the deep over it, and I held back its rivers, and the many waters were restrained; and I clothed Lebanon in gloom for it, and all the trees of the field fainted over it.

R.15: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: On the day it went down to the grave, I made the deep waters mourn for it. I covered it with the deep and held back its rivers, so that the great waters stopped flowing. I made the Lebanon mountains mourn for it, and all the trees in the field withered because of it.

decisions.choice: Sheol: the world of the dead
decisions.reason: Sheol is the place below where all the dead were pictured as gathered (Isaiah 14:9). Ezekiel names it here and in verses 16-17 and 32:21, 27.

decisions.choice: I caused mourning; I covered the deep over it
alternatives: I covered the deep in mourning for it
decisions.reason: The two verbs stand side by side. The deep that fed the tree goes into mourning, as if veiled, or covers the fallen tree. The waters that made it grow are stopped.

decisions.choice: the grave (R); Sheol (L, B)
decisions.reason: Sheol follows the Isaiah table: Literal and Balanced keep the name, Readable says "the grave". "The pit" stays at every level, as in 26:20.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The settled formula.

records.heading: Down to Sheol

records.source: מִקּ֤וֹל מַפַּלְתּוֹ֙ הִרְעַ֣שְׁתִּי גוֹיִ֔ם בְּהוֹרִדִ֥י אֹת֛וֹ שְׁא֖וֹלָה אֶת־י֣וֹרְדֵי ב֑וֹר וַיִּנָּ֨חֲמ֜וּ בְּאֶ֤רֶץ תַּחְתִּית֙ כָּל־עֲצֵי־עֵ֔דֶן מִבְחַ֥ר וְטוֹב־לְבָנ֖וֹן כָּל־שֹׁ֥תֵי מָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: From [the] sound of its downfall I made nations quake, when I brought it down to Sheol with [those who] go down [to the] pit; and were comforted in [the] earth below all [the] trees of Eden, the choice and best of Lebanon, all drinkers of water.
pieces: I made the nations shake at the sound of its fall, when I brought it down to Sheol with those who go down to the pit. Then in the world below all the trees of Eden took comfort, the choicest and best of Lebanon, every tree that drinks water.

L.16: At the sound of its downfall I made the nations quake, when I brought it down to Sheol with those who go down to the pit; and all the trees of Eden were comforted in the earth below, the choice and best of Lebanon, all that drink water.

R.16: The nations shook with fear when they heard the noise of its fall, when I brought it down to the grave with those who go down to the pit. Then all the trees of Eden, the finest and best trees of Lebanon, all the trees that had plenty of water, were comforted in the world below.

decisions.choice: the trees of Eden were comforted: the fallen great ones take comfort
decisions.reason: The trees already in the world below, the kings and nations that fell before, are consoled that the greatest of them has joined them (32:31; compare Isaiah 14:9-10).

decisions.choice: the grave (R); Sheol (L, B)
decisions.reason: Sheol follows the Isaiah table: Literal and Balanced keep the name, Readable says "the grave". "The pit" stays at every level, as in 26:20.

records.source: גַּם־הֵ֗ם אִתּ֛וֹ יָרְד֥וּ שְׁא֖וֹלָה אֶל־חַלְלֵי־חָ֑רֶב וּזְרֹע֛וֹ יָשְׁב֥וּ בְצִלּ֖וֹ בְּת֥וֹךְ גּוֹיִֽם׃
records.gloss: Also they with it went down to Sheol, to [those] slain by [the] sword, and its arm, [who] dwelt in its shade in [the] midst of [the] nations.
pieces: They too went down with it to Sheol, to those killed by the sword, along with those who were its strength, who had lived in its shade among the nations.

L.17: They also went down with it to Sheol, to those slain by the sword, and [those who were] its arm, who dwelt in its shade in the midst of the nations.

R.17: Those who were its allies and lived in its shade among the nations also went down with it to the grave, to join those who were killed in war.

decisions.choice: its arm: its strength, its allies
decisions.reason: The arm is strength (30:21-25); here those who were the tree's strength, its allies and helpers. The Greek translation reads "its seed" (stated from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: those slain by the sword: those who died violent deaths
decisions.reason: In Ezekiel's picture of the world of the dead they lie in a place of disgrace (32:20-32).

decisions.choice: the grave (R); Sheol (L, B)
decisions.reason: Sheol follows the Isaiah table: Literal and Balanced keep the name, Readable says "the grave". "The pit" stays at every level, as in 26:20.

records.source: אֶל־מִ֨י דָמִ֥יתָ כָּ֛כָה בְּכָב֥וֹד וּבְגֹ֖דֶל בַּעֲצֵי־עֵ֑דֶן וְהוּרַדְתָּ֨אֶת־עֲצֵי־עֵ֜דֶן אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ תַּחְתִּ֗ית בְּת֨וֹךְ עֲרֵלִ֤ים תִּשְׁכַּב֙ אֶת־חַלְלֵי־חֶ֔רֶב ה֤וּא פַרְעֹה֙ וְכָל־הֲמוֹנֹ֔הנְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה׃ס
records.gloss: To whom are you thus like in glory and in greatness among [the] trees of Eden? And you will be brought down with [the] trees of Eden to [the] earth below; in [the] midst of [the] uncircumcised you will lie, with [those] slain by [the] sword. This [is] Pharaoh and all his multitude, declaration of [the] Lord Yahweh.
pieces: Which of the trees of Eden was like you in glory and greatness? Yet you too will be brought down with the trees of Eden into the world below. You will lie among the uncircumcised, with those killed by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his hordes, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.18: To whom are you like, so, in glory and in greatness among the trees of Eden? But you will be brought down along with the trees of Eden into the earth below; in the midst of the uncircumcised you will lie, with the slain of the sword. That [is] Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.18: Pharaoh, which of the trees of Eden was as great and splendid as you? But you too will be brought down with the trees of Eden into the world below. You will lie among the uncircumcised, who die in disgrace, with those killed in war. This is what will happen to Pharaoh and all his crowds of people, says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the question of verse 2 answered
decisions.reason: Pharaoh asked to compare himself with the great cedar; he will share its fall.

decisions.choice: among the uncircumcised: in disgrace
decisions.reason: See 28:10. The theme is taken up at length in 32:19-32.

decisions.choice: this is Pharaoh: the picture explained
decisions.reason: The last words apply the parable: the tree that fell is a picture of Pharaoh and his people.

decisions.choice: who die in disgrace
decisions.reason: Readable says what lying among the uncircumcised means, as at 28:10.

decisions.choice: declares the Lord GOD (L, B); says the Lord GOD (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording for *ne'um Adonai YHWH* in Ezekiel.
